hook: "some app brands' marketing looks like a niche page you'd follow even if you never downloaded the app."
body: The thesis: the best app marketing looks like a niche page you'd follow anyway ('5 dinners for when you're too tired to cook'). The slideshow gives value before the product appears. The recipe-app build: slide 1 hook ('3 dinners for when the fridge is almost empty'), slides 2-4 the meals, slide 5 screen recording of saving, slide 6 finished meal + next step. Then give the clipping team situations (cheap dinners, quick lunches, cooking for one) — same product, different reasons to care. The warning: if the app is just a logo at the end, people save and never download — the product needs a ROLE.
cta: "if you're building an app, reply with what it does. i'll give you a slideshow angle i'd test." — reply-gated free consulting.
idea: Niche-page slideshows earn attention with usefulness before the product appears — but the product must have a ROLE in the story, not just a logo at the end, or viewers save without converting.
sequencing: Hook: marketing that looks like a niche page.
Example hooks: 3 useful slideshows.
The insight: useful first, product later.
The build: 6-slide recipe-app structure.
The scale: clipping team × situations.
The warning: logo-at-end = saves without downloads.
The rule: the product needs a role.
CTA: reply for a free angle.
formatting: Thesis + build spec: example hooks, a 6-slide structure, the clipping-team brief, the warning. Consultant-voice post.
why_it_works: 'You'd follow even if you never downloaded' sets the quality bar as follow-worthiness. The save-without-download warning names the exact failure mode of value-first content.
what_to_steal: The golden rule for LC's meme/slideshow lane: 'the format earns the attention, the product still needs a role.' LC's jewelry slideshows: styling tip slides → the LC piece as the solution step (not a logo at the end). The 6-slide structure ports directly: hook → tips → LC piece in use → finished look + shop step.
